      85                 :             : /// \brief Fixed-capacity vector whose capacity is set on construction and never changed.
      86                 :             : ///
      87                 :             : /// The NonRelocatableVector is a std::vector-like structure which guarantees that no reallocation will ever be made (so
      88                 :             : /// pointers or references to elements will never be invalidated. Memory for the capacity specified is allocated on
      89                 :             : /// construction and each element is initialised when inserting an element (e.g. via emplace_back).
      90                 :             : ///
      91                 :             : /// \details The implementation also provides some "performance optimizations" in its iterator handling:
      92                 :             : /// It makes sure to return "raw-pointers" as its begin/end-iterators. E.g. independent from the pointer-type, the
      93                 :             : /// underlying Allocator provides, it doesn't return these pointer-types 1:1 as begin/end iterator, but returns
      94                 :             : /// raw-pointers instead. This is a performance benefit, when we use DynamicArray in shared-memory, where we use
      95                 :             : /// score::memory::shared::PolymorphicOffsetPtrAllocator as our allocator, which creates fancy OffsetPtr.
      96                 :             : /// Dereferencing an OffsetPtr is expensive as it applies bounds-checking for safety-reasons. But when iterating over
      97                 :             : /// a DynamicArray residing in shared-memory, doing a bounds-check for every element is unnecessary. Only the 1st/last
      98                 :             : /// OffsetPtr needs to be checked. This is exactly the iterator optimization applied here: Only the start/end gets
      99                 :             : /// bounds-checked and if this is successful a raw-pointer is handed out as an iterator.
